newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar holds strength but more muted PM.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar holds strength but more muted PM.

text.p: White sugar futures built on their recent gains on Thursday afternoon but activity on the whites was limited in light of the rangebound performance in New York, traders said.
A lacklustre trading session on July raws between 11.15 and 11.22 cents/lb partly helped to dampen sentiment in London, despite the healthy volume and general firmness across the board, they said.
"With London being up around $1.40 we were hoping it might do something reasonable...but you've got a seven point range basis July (raws)," said one.
"It's petered out a little bit -- it's all a bit full despite the reasonable volume," he said.
Commission house crosses were cited as boosting the overall volume, which by 1615 GMT stood at a hefty 3,519 lots -- mostly in August, although October and December also commanded healthy interest.
August was up $1.60 at $322.80 and October up $2.00 at $312.50. Other positions were slightly firmer.
Technically, August has continued to push higher and has created a new upward trendline dating from a mid-February high of $312.00.
Analaysts said the spot position was well supported by short-term moving averages and a band of trading between $310 and $315.
August/October narrowed to just over $10.00 after the $10.60 seen during Wednesday's session and December/March was also active during earlier trading, sources said.
A limited number of against actuals trades was cited along with some options interest. August puts were seen at strikes of $320 and December puts at $300 and $310.
The Paris market was also firmer and 425 lots were traded. August was up $1.90 at $323.00 and October up 40 cents at $311.00.
